chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the time of Zuhr. He said: One cubit from the sun’s decline; and the time of 'Asr is one cubit from the time of Zuhr, so that is four feet from the sun’s decline.

And Zurarah said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said to me when I asked him about that: The wall of the مسجد of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was one stature high, so when one cubit of its shadow had passed, he would perform Zuhr; and when two cubits of its shadow had passed, he would perform 'Asr. Then he said: Do you know why one cubit and two cubits were assigned? I said: Why was that assigned? He said: Because of the obligatory prayer, for you may perform supererogatory prayers from the sun’s decline until the shadow passes one cubit. Then when your shadow reaches one cubit from the decline, you begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the supererogatory prayer.

Ibn Muskan said: And Sulayman ibn Khalid, Abu Basir al-Muradi, Husayn the companion of al-Qalanisi, Ibn Abi Ya'fur, and others among them whom I cannot enumerate, narrated to me regarding the one cubit and the two cubits.

So if it is said: How is it possible for you to act upon these reports despite the variation in their wording and the contradiction in their meanings? Because some of them mention the stature, some mention the cubit, and some mention the foot, and these are different measures. We say: These expressions, even if they differ, their meaning is not different, because the stature is an expression for the cubit, as we shall explain later; thus both are two expressions for one thing. And the mention of the two feet corresponds to them, while what has come in some reports mentioning one foot applies to one who lightens his supererogatory prayers, because what is taken into consideration in that is the amount in which the supererogatory prayers are performed, whether little or much; except that this must not exceed the measure of a cubit, a stature, or two feet, and whatever is less than that is sufficient. What indicates that is what we have previously presented from the reports, from his saying to 'Umar ibn Hanzalah, Mansur ibn Hazim, al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah, and others: That is up to you; if you wish you may lengthen, and if you wish you may shorten. So when you finish your supererogatory prayers, you perform the obligatory prayer. And what indicates that the stature is an expression for the cubit and the two feet...

key_terms.الْقَامَةِ: a stature used as a measure corresponding in meaning here
key_terms.الْقَدَمَيْنِ: two feet as a reported measure corresponding to the same timing principle
key_terms.ذِرَاعٌ: a cubit used as a measure of shadow length
key_terms.وَقْتِ الظُّهْرِ: the beginning time of the Zuhr prayer

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith define the beginning time of Zuhr and 'Asr prayers using shadow measurements?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the beginning times of Zuhr and 'Asr in relation to the sun’s decline and the measured extension of shadow. It also explains that differing expressions in the reports—such as cubit, stature, and foot—can refer to the same practical ruling regarding the time allotted for supererogatory prayer before the obligatory salat.
